content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim against the evidence. The root-cause claim rests on one reading of the code, so I'm keeping it marked as unverified, and I'm tracing how the monthly spend summary gets called once account pages move to the new renderer.

I'm checking the remaining claims against the evidence: the fallback being unsafe to switch off, the 37.5% error rate at 03:39, and the division-by-zero in the spend summary code. The claim that the error came from the new renderer is only partly backed, since the log line itself doesn't name the renderer, so I'm leaning on the renderer comparison and the rollback results to support it.

I'm going through the remaining claims that depend on the logs and flag toggles, noting which ones are only partly supported. Two flags changed at the same moment, so the investigation couldn't separate their effects, and the first flag it blamed was later ruled out. I'm also checking whether the test suite would have caught this, and noting that no one was paged.

I'm checking the last few claims against the log lines and code: the division by the number of purchases this month, which fails when that list is empty, and the claim that nobody was paged. The remaining points rest on facts already confirmed earlier, so they hold.

supported.quote: Once account pages went through the new renderer, its monthly spend summary called average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total by the number of purchases made this month and has no guard for an empty list. So it raises ZeroDivisionError for every shopper who has bought nothing this month, and serve_account_page turns that into a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

Switching off an older fallback sent shoppers' account pages through a newer way of building them, and that newer way likely breaks for any shopper who has bought nothing this month, because it divides by that month's number of purchases.
Switching the legacy checkout fallback off again, or anything else that sends account pages to the new renderer, could make account pages fail again for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.
Shoppers' account pages failed to load

It did not change what was done first: the investigation weighed it as refuted and Argus reverted monthly-spend-feature first, and the flag the lead named was switched back on only as the second candidate, which turned out to be the action that put the service back.
Shoppers' account page requests failed far more often than before.
The failed requests broke on a division-by-zero error raised while the page's spend summary was being built.
The error came from the new renderer, which had started serving account pages that the legacy renderer had served until then.
Pages moved to the new renderer because the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off.

The switch-on of the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at the same instant (P2): the service stayed at the incident's level with it turned off again, and it was back to normal with it on once the fallback was restored.
The new renderer's monthly per-item spend average divides by zero, and the reading of the code puts this down to shoppers with no purchases this month.
The legacy fallback was switched off for all account-page traffic at once. No check was seen that the path it exposed, the new renderer, worked first, and no staged rollout was seen.
Two feature flags were changed at the same instant, so the investigation could not tell their effects apart and blamed the wrong flag first.
No test was seen for the monthly spend average with a shopper who has bought nothing this month.
The error-rate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
